issues.legal_issue: The residual limitation period for applications does not govern an application to file an arbitration agreement when the application is made under a separate arbitration law and no law extends that residual period to it.
material_facts: The parties had a written agreement containing an arbitration clause, and an assignee of the original contractor sought to have the agreement filed and the disputes referred to arbitration.
The disputes arose in 1950, while the application to file the agreement was made in 1955; the opposing party argued that the application was out of time.
The lower appellate court applied the residual limitation period for applications and treated the period as running from when the differences arose.
issues.conclusion: The residual limitation article did not govern the application to file the arbitration agreement, and the application was not barred under that article.
issues.legal_principle: Article 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908, was construed as applying to applications under the Code of Civil Procedure for which no period was otherwise prescribed, consistent with the line of authority including Bai Manekbai v. Manekji Kayasji, Hansraj Gupta v. Official Liquidators of the Dehradun-Mussoorie Electric Tramway Company Ltd., Sha Mulchand & Company Ltd. v. Jawahar Mills Ltd., and Bombay Gas Company Ltd. v. Gopal Bhiva. The amendments to Articles 158 and 178 made by the Arbitration Act, 1940, did not alter the established meaning of Article 181. Section 37(1) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, did not extend Article 181 to an application to file an arbitration agreement.

predicates.is_application_to_file_arbitration_agree: A party applied to a court to file a written arbitration agreement and obtain a reference of the dispute to arbitration.
predicates.is_made_under_separate_arbitration_law: The application was made under a law governing arbitration rather than under the general civil procedure code.
predicates.no_rule_extends_residual_application_lim: No applicable rule expressly or by clear implication extended the residual limitation period for applications to this kind of application.

issues.definition: When a party applies under a separate arbitration law to file an arbitration agreement, and no rule extends the residual application limit to that filing, the application is not barred by that residual limit.

issues.legal_issue: In an application to file an arbitration agreement and refer a dispute, the court must leave the limitation of the underlying claim to the arbitrator rather than reject the application on that ground.
material_facts: The applicants sought to file a written arbitration agreement and refer disputes concerning rights under that agreement to its named arbitrator.
The opposing party argued that the underlying disputes had arisen years before the application and were therefore time-barred.
The agreement was treated as a valid, subsisting written agreement made before the institution of any suit, and the disputes concerned its subject matter.
issues.conclusion: The court was not to decide whether the underlying claims were time-barred when considering the application; that question was for the arbitrator after the reference. The court had to determine whether a valid, subsisting written agreement existed, whether a dispute within its subject matter had arisen, and whether the dispute was within the court's jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 20 and 37(1) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, Section 37(1) requires limitation law to be applied in the arbitration to the dispute referred, but does not authorize the court to refuse an application to file an arbitration agreement because the underlying claim may be time-barred. Section 37(1) reflects the principle discussed in Ramdutt Ramkissendass v. F.D. Sasson and Company that an arbitrator decides according to the law applicable to the dispute. At the filing-and-reference stage, the court must examine the existence of a valid and subsisting written agreement executed before any suit, a dispute within the agreement's subject matter, and the court's jurisdiction.

predicates.written_agreement_is_valid_and_subsistin: The parties had a written arbitration agreement that remained valid and in force.

issues.definition: When a court considers an application to file and refer a dispute under a valid, subsisting, pre-suit written agreement, and the dispute falls within the agreement and the court's jurisdiction, the court leaves limitation of the underlying claim to the arbitrator.
